## 1. One-paragraph verdict
Genuine CBR MP3 fixture, name-faithful: `file` → "ID3 version 2.3.0, contains: MPEG ADTS, layer III, v1, **128 kbps, 44.1 kHz, Stereo**"; ffprobe → codec mp3, 44100 Hz, stereo, 2.04 s. My independent ffmpeg decode produces s16le MD5 `253c926ff193cfe2db3a5b092acba2f4`, exactly the `ffmpeg_pcm_md5` recorded for `[fixture.cbr128]` in tests/data/mp3_bitexact_reference.txt:47 — and the same digest the reference records for the `tagged_art` fixture (line 97, "same PCM essence as cbr128 behind a tag"), confirming that documented relationship too.

## 2. What actually works (verified)
- file/ffprobe facts == name (CBR 128, 44.1k stereo).
- `ffmpeg -i cbr128.mp3 -map 0:a -c:a pcm_s16le -f s16le - | md5sum` → `253c926ff193cfe2db3a5b092acba2f4` == mp3_bitexact_reference.txt:47 (sed-verified); matches tagged_art row :97 as documented.
- Consumers: mp3_bitexact.rs (incl. the tag-skip-neutrality test :110-113), mp3_bench, mp3_corpus_differential, mp3_fuzz_survival.
